mapmc-fmc-2024-p1.title: Count around the edge
mapmc-fmc-2024-p1.body:
Put your finger on one corner and go around the shape, counting each straight side until you are back where you started: there are 5 sides (it is a pentagon).

**Answer: (B) 5**

mapmc-fmc-2024-01.title: Start from 20
mapmc-fmc-2024-01.body:
Pairs that multiply to 20: $1 \times 20$, $2 \times 10$, $4 \times 5$. Only 4 and 5 add to 9.

**Answer: (E) 4 and 5**

mapmc-fmc-2024-02.title: Double it
mapmc-fmc-2024-02.body:
6 km is twice 3 km, so it takes twice as long: 2 hours.

**Answer: (A) 2 hours**

mapmc-fmc-2024-02.title: Hour by hour
mapmc-fmc-2024-02.body:
After 1 hour she has walked 3 km; after 2 hours, $3 + 3 = 6$ km. Done!

**Answer: (A) 2 hours**

mapmc-fmc-2024-03.title: Check both rules
mapmc-fmc-2024-03.body:
- A (5, 31, 31) and B (7, 30, 30) repeat a number, so they are not all different.
- B and E (13, 20, 34) contain even numbers.
- C: $9 + 27 + 33 = 69$. ✗
- D: $11 + 27 + 29 = 67$ ✓, and 11, 27, 29 are different and odd.

**Answer: (D) 11, 27, 29**

mapmc-fmc-2024-03.title: Add the candidates
mapmc-fmc-2024-03.body:
Only C and D are three different odd numbers. $9 + 27 + 33 = 69$, while $11 + 27 + 29 = 38 + 29 = 67$.

**Answer: (D) 11, 27, 29**

mapmc-fmc-2024-04.title: Star first
mapmc-fmc-2024-04.body:
$3 + \bigstar = 25$, so the star is $25 - 3 = 22$. Then $22 - \triangle = 5$, so the triangle is $22 - 5 = 17$.

**Answer: (E) 17**

mapmc-fmc-2024-04.title: Check the options
mapmc-fmc-2024-04.body:
The star is 22. Try the triangle: $22 - 13 = 9$, $22 - 15 = 7$, $22 - 17 = 5$ ✓.

**Answer: (E) 17**

mapmc-fmc-2024-05.title: Count groups of 5
mapmc-fmc-2024-05.body:
Flora has one group of 5 and Istry has three groups of 5: four groups of 5 altogether, $4 \times 5 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

mapmc-fmc-2024-06.title: Small ones, then big ones
mapmc-fmc-2024-06.body:
- Small triangles: the bottom row has 5 and the top row has 3, so 8.
- Bigger triangles made of 4 small ones: one with its top at the left top corner and one with its top at the right top corner — 2 more.

Total: $8 + 2 = 10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

mapmc-fmc-2024-06.title: Count by size and direction
mapmc-fmc-2024-06.body:
Pointing up: 5 small + 2 big = 7. Pointing down: 3 small (and no big ones, because the top edge is too short). $7 + 3 = 10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

mapmc-fmc-2024-07.title: Step by step
mapmc-fmc-2024-07.body:
- 1 bucket = 5 bottles = $5 \times 4 = 20$ jugs.
- The pond = 10 buckets = $10 \times 20 = 200$ jugs.

**Answer: (E) 200**

mapmc-fmc-2024-07.title: Bottles first
mapmc-fmc-2024-07.body:
The pond takes $10 \times 5 = 50$ milk bottles, and each bottle is 4 jugs: $50 \times 4 = 200$ jugs.

**Answer: (E) 200**

mapmc-fmc-2024-08.title: Same years pass for both
mapmc-fmc-2024-08.body:
From my 7th to my 14th birthday is 7 years. My father also gets 7 years older: $35 + 7 = 42$.

**Answer: (B) 42**

mapmc-fmc-2024-08.title: Age gap
mapmc-fmc-2024-08.body:
My father is $35 - 7 = 28$ years older than me, always. When I am 14 he is $14 + 28 = 42$. (Doubling 35 to 70 is the trap!)

**Answer: (B) 42**

mapmc-fmc-2024-09.title: Take away the extras
mapmc-fmc-2024-09.body:
The four sides are: shortest, shortest + 1, shortest + 2, shortest + 3. The extras add up to $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$ cm. So 4 shortest sides make $46 - 6 = 40$ cm, and the shortest side is $40 \div 4 = 10$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 10**

mapmc-fmc-2024-10.title: Count the legs
mapmc-fmc-2024-10.body:
Cow legs: $20 \times 4 = 80$. So the chickens have 80 legs, and with 2 legs each there are $80 \div 2 = 40$ chickens. Animals: $20 + 40 = 60$.

**Answer: (D) 60**

mapmc-fmc-2024-10.title: Two chickens per cow
mapmc-fmc-2024-10.body:
One cow has 4 legs, the same as 2 chickens. So for every cow there are 2 chickens: $2 \times 20 = 40$ chickens, and $20 + 40 = 60$ animals.

**Answer: (D) 60**

mapmc-fmc-2024-11.title: Bar model
mapmc-fmc-2024-11.body:
Adding 15 to the number gives 4 lots of the number. So 15 must be the other 3 lots of the number: $15 \div 3 = 5$.

**Answer: (B) 5**

mapmc-fmc-2024-12.title: Measure in red squares
mapmc-fmc-2024-12.body:
The red X is made of 5 equal tilted squares. The white parts around it are 4 triangles that are each half a red square, and 4 corner triangles that are each a quarter of a red square: $4 \times \frac12 + 4 \times \frac14 = 2 + 1 = 3$ red squares. So the whole diagram is $5 + 3 = 8$ red squares, and $\frac58$ is shaded.

**Answer: (B) $\frac58$**

mapmc-fmc-2024-12.title: Use quarters of the big square
mapmc-fmc-2024-12.body:
Each red square's corners touch the middle of the sides of a box that is a quarter of the big square (half as wide and half as tall), so each red square fills half of that quarter: $\frac12 \times \frac14 = \frac18$ of the diagram. Five red squares: $\frac58$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac58$**

mapmc-fmc-2024-13.title: Count and halve
mapmc-fmc-2024-13.body:
5 choices for the first topping and 4 for the second: $5 \times 4 = 20$. But each pair has been counted twice (ham then pineapple is the same as pineapple then ham), so $20 \div 2 = 10$.

**Answer: (E) 10**

mapmc-fmc-2024-14.title: Look at the units column
mapmc-fmc-2024-14.body:
Three equal digits add up to something ending in 8. $3 \times 6 = 18$ is the only one that works (3 × 4 = 12, 3 × 5 = 15, 3 × 7 = 21, 3 × 8 = 24). Check: $66 + 66 + 66 = 198$ ✓.

**Answer: (C) 6**

mapmc-fmc-2024-14.title: Divide by 3
mapmc-fmc-2024-14.body:
The three numbers are equal, so each is $198 \div 3 = 66$. Both digits are 6.

**Answer: (C) 6**

mapmc-fmc-2024-15.title: Find the burning time
mapmc-fmc-2024-15.body:
Only $15 - 1 = 14$ cm can burn. At 2 cm per hour that takes $14 \div 2 = 7$ hours. 7 hours after 11 am is 6 pm.

**Answer: (E) 6 pm**

mapmc-fmc-2024-15.title: Hour by hour
mapmc-fmc-2024-15.body:
15 cm at 11 am, 13 at 12 noon, 11 at 1 pm, 9 at 2 pm, 7 at 3 pm, 5 at 4 pm, 3 at 5 pm, 1 cm at 6 pm — only the part in the candlestick is left.

**Answer: (E) 6 pm**

mapmc-fmc-2024-16.title: Boys first
mapmc-fmc-2024-16.body:
Boys: $35 - 20 = 15$. Boys who can read music: $20 - 14 = 6$. Boys who cannot: $15 - 6 = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

mapmc-fmc-2024-16.title: Children who can't read music
mapmc-fmc-2024-16.body:
$35 - 20 = 15$ children cannot read music. Girls who cannot: $20 - 14 = 6$. So boys who cannot: $15 - 6 = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

mapmc-fmc-2024-17.title: Digit sum
mapmc-fmc-2024-17.body:
A number divides by 3 exactly when its digit sum does. The digits of 2024 add to $2 + 0 + 2 + 4 = 8$. Adding 4 makes the sum go up by 4: $8 + 4 = 12$, which is in the 3 times table. (Adding 5, 6, 8 or 9 gives 13, 14, 16 or 17 — none divide by 3.) Check: $2028 = 3 \times 676$.

**Answer: (A) 4**

mapmc-fmc-2024-17.title: Remainders
mapmc-fmc-2024-17.body:
$2024 = 3 \times 674 + 2$, so 2024 is 2 more than a multiple of 3. We need to add 1, 4, 7, … to reach the next multiple. Of the choices only 4 works.

**Answer: (A) 4**

mapmc-fmc-2024-18.title: Take away the total at once

mapmc-fmc-2024-19.title: Count squares
mapmc-fmc-2024-19.body:
The grid has $4 \times 4 = 16$ squares. Tiles A (2 squares), B, D and E (4 squares each) all have a number of squares that goes exactly into 16. Tile C has 3 squares, and 16 is not in the 3 times table, so copies of C can never cover exactly 16 squares.

**Answer: (C)**

mapmc-fmc-2024-19.title: Show the others work
mapmc-fmc-2024-19.body:
- A: 8 dominoes, two in each row.
- B: 4 straight tiles, one in each row.
- D: two L tiles (one turned upside down) fit together into a 2-by-4 rectangle, and two such rectangles fill the grid.
- E: four T tiles, one lying along each side of the grid with its bump pointing inwards, fit together like a pinwheel.

So C is the only tile that cannot work.

**Answer: (C)**

mapmc-fmc-2024-20.title: Place Sam and Peter
mapmc-fmc-2024-20.body:
Sam and Peter stand together (Sam, then Peter), and Thelma is somewhere behind Peter. Ramesh takes place 4, so only place 5 is behind him. Thelma must be behind Peter, so Sam and Peter are in places 1–2 or 2–3. Qureshi is ahead of Peter — and must not be between Sam and Peter — so Qureshi is ahead of Sam too: Qureshi, Sam, Peter, Ramesh, Thelma.

**Answer: (B) Qureshi**

mapmc-fmc-2024-20.title: Check the order
mapmc-fmc-2024-20.body:
Qureshi 1st, Sam 2nd, Peter 3rd, Ramesh 4th, Thelma 5th: Ramesh is 4th ✓, Peter right after Sam ✓ and before Thelma ✓, Qureshi ahead of Peter ✓.

**Answer: (B) Qureshi**
